Generate a Target Population for Simulation

Source: R/pmgen_target_pop.R
pmgen_target_population.Rd

Partitions the joint predictor distribution stored in a pmgen_ref_model object into two non-overlapping sets: a fixed target population of size n (used to evaluate each simulated model) and a development pool containing all remaining rows (used to draw development datasets in pmgen_simulate()).

Usage

pmgen_target_population(ref_model, n = 100000L, dev_pool_n = NULL, seed = NULL)

Arguments

ref_model

A pmgen_ref_model object from pmgen_reference().

n

Integer. Number of individuals in the target population. Must be strictly less than nrow(ref_model$joint_data). Default 100000.

dev_pool_n

Integer or NULL. If NULL (default), the development pool contains all rows of joint_data not selected for the target population. If an integer, only that many rows are retained in the pool (sampled from the remainder). Useful when memory is limited or when intentionally bounding the available development data.

seed

Integer or NULL. Random seed.

Value

A pmgen_target_pop object with slots:

  • $data: target population data frame (predictors, lp, p_true, outcome)

  • $dev_pool: development pool data frame (predictors only; outcomes are generated fresh each simulation draw in pmgen_simulate())

  • $ref_model, $n, $seed

Details

The target population rows are sampled without replacement from joint_data, so the two sets are guaranteed to be disjoint. The reference model is applied to the target population rows to compute true predicted risks and simulated binary outcomes.

References

Riley RD, Whittle R, Sadatsafavi M, Martin GP, Pate A, Collins GS, Ensor J. A general sample size framework for developing or updating a predictive algorithm: with application to clinical prediction models. BMC Medical Research Methodology. 2026;26:121. doi:10.1186/s12874-026-02856-7

Examples

# Small settings so the example runs quickly; see pmgen_reference()
ref <- pmgen_reference(
  joint_data = dvt_data, predictors = setdiff(names(dvt_data), "dvt"),
  prevalence = 0.21, cstatistic = 0.78,
  n_bisect_pop = 1e5, n_synth = 1e5, seed = 42
)
#> Running bisection to calibrate reference model...
#> Bisection converged: prevalence=0.2100 (target=0.2100), c-stat=0.7791 (target=0.7800)
#> Unit information matrix computed and cached.
tp <- pmgen_target_population(ref, n = 5000, seed = 42)
tp
#> pmgen target population
#> -----------------------
#>   Target pop N    : 5000
#>   Dev pool N      : 4805
#>   Seed            : 42
#>   Prevalence (observed): 0.2088
#>   Mean true risk  : 0.2150
#>   Predictors      : male, OCuse, malignancy, surgery, ab_leg_trauma, vein_distension, calf_diff, ab_ddimer, pregnancy, immobile, clotting
